words.gloss: she who is the property (wife) of another

ai.literal: The folly of desiring and behaving (inappropriately) with her who is the property of another, in this world, among those who have seen the meaning of virtue, does not exist.
ai.translation: The folly of desiring and lusting after another man's wife does not exist in this world among those who have understood the true nature of virtue and wealth.
ai.modern: பிறனுடைய மனைவியை விரும்பி ஒழுகும் அறியாமை, அறத்தின் மற்றும் பொருளின் உண்மையான இயல்பை உணர்ந்தவர்களிடம் இவ்வுலகில் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that desiring another person's wife, referred to here as 'பிறன்பொருளாள்' (one who is the partner or property of another), is a form of supreme ignorance or folly ('பேதைமை'). Those who have truly understood the essence of virtue ('அறம்') and the true value of life's pursuits ('பொருள்') will never possess this foolish desire. The poet asserts that such a base desire is entirely absent ('இல்') among wise and righteous people in this world ('ஞாலத்து'). By choosing 'பொருளாள்' to mean a wife who is a man's rightful partner, the text emphasizes the violation of social and moral boundaries.

ai.literal: Among all those who stood outside virtue, than those who stood at another's gate, fools there are none.
ai.translation: Among all those who stray from the path of virtue, there are no greater fools than those who stand at another man's gate desiring his wife.
ai.modern: அறநெறிக்கு வெளியே நிற்பவர்கள் எல்லாரிலும், பிறனுடைய வாசலில் (அவன் மனைவியை விரும்பி) நிற்பவர்களை விட அறிவிலிகள் யாரும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet highlights the extreme foolishness of desiring another man's wife. The poet compares various wrongdoers—those who have abandoned virtue and stand at its outer limits ('அறன்கடை')—and declares that none among them are as foolish as the person who stands at another's threshold ('பிறன்கடை') with lustful intent. The word 'கடை' is used masterfully in two senses: first as the lowest state or outside of virtue, and second as the physical threshold of another's house. This comparison emphasizes that violating another's domestic trust is the ultimate height of ignorance and self-destruction.

words.gloss: in the home of those who trusted them

ai.literal: Than those who are dead, different they are not, surely, who in the home of those who trusted them, evil having done, conduct themselves.
ai.translation: Those who act wickedly by violating the trust of those who confided in them are surely no different from the dead.
ai.modern: தம்மை நம்பியவர்களுடைய இல்லத்தில் தீமை செய்து வாழ்பவர்கள், இறந்தவர்களை விட வேறுபட்டவர்கள் அல்லர்; அவர்கள் பிணத்திற்கு ஒப்பானவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the severe moral degradation of violating another's trust. The word 'தெளிந்தார்' refers to those who have placed complete trust in a person, and 'இல்' refers to their home or wife. Anyone who enters such a household and commits the ultimate betrayal of desiring the wife is said to be 'விளிந்தாரின் வேறல்லர்'—no different from a dead person. Although they are physically alive, their complete loss of virtue and honor renders them equivalent to a corpse.

words.gloss: even to the tiny measure of a millet seed

ai.literal: Of whatever greatness they may be, what is the use, if, even a millet-seed's measure not reflecting, another's house they enter?
ai.translation: Of what use is any degree of greatness they may possess, if, without reflecting even to the measure of a tiny millet seed, they enter another's home with desire?
ai.modern: எவ்வளவு பெருமை உடையவராக இருந்தாலும், தினை அளவு கூட ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காமல் பிறனுடைய வீட்டிற்குள் (அவன் மனைவியை விரும்பி) நுழைந்தால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet warns that no amount of power, learning, or social stature can save a person's reputation if they lack moral restraint. The phrase 'தினைத்துணையும் தேரான்' describes someone who fails to reflect on the consequences of their actions even to the tiny extent of a millet seed. 'பிறனில் புகல்' refers to entering another man's home with lustful intent toward his wife. The author emphasizes that this single, unthinking act of transgression completely nullifies all of one's accumulated greatness.

ai.literal: Thinking it is easy, he who transgresses another's home, will always attain a disgrace that stands without dying.
ai.translation: He who enters another's home coveting his wife, thinking it is an easy deed, will acquire a disgrace that stands forever without dying.
ai.modern: இது எளிய செயல் என்று நினைத்துப் பிறனுடைய வீட்டிற்குள் நுழைந்து தவறு செய்பவன், எப்போதும் அழியாமல் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் பழியை அடைவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the grave error of desiring another's wife. A person might trespass into another's home ('இல்') thinking it is an easy ('எளிது') or trivial matter to escape caught. However, the consequence of this transgression ('இறப்பான்') is a permanent, undying disgrace ('விளியாது நிற்கும் பழி') that will follow them for all time ('எஞ்ஞான்றும்').

ai.literal: Enmity, sin, fear, and blame—these four indeed will not depart from him who transgresses another's home.
ai.translation: Enmity, sin, fear, and disgrace—these four things will never leave the man who trespasses into another's home.
ai.modern: பிறனுடைய இல்லற எல்லையைக் கடந்து தவறு செய்பவனிடமிருந்து பகை, பாவம், அச்சம், பழி ஆகிய நான்கு குணங்களும் நீங்கவே மாட்டா.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the severe consequences of violating the sanctity of another person's home. The poet uses the compound 'ill-iṟappāṉ' to describe one who transgresses or trespasses into another's household. Such a person is permanently accompanied by four evils: enmity from others, the spiritual burden of sin, constant fear of discovery, and public disgrace. The word 'ikavā' emphasizes that these four consequences are inseparable and will never leave the wrongdoer.

he who lives in a household

ai.literal: He who is called a householder living by the nature of virtue is he who does not desire the womanhood of her who belongs to another.
ai.translation: He who is said to live a virtuous householder's life is one who does not lust after the womanhood of another man's wife.
ai.modern: அறநெறியோடு இல்வாழ்க்கை வாழ்பவன் என்று சொல்லப்படுபவன், பிறனுடைய மனைவியின் பெண்மையை விரும்பாதவனே ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true standard of a virtuous householder. A person who is praised as living a righteous domestic life must possess the self-control to not covet another man's wife. The word 'piṟaṉiyalāḷ' refers to a woman who belongs to another man's household. By stating that such a householder does not desire her womanhood, the poet emphasizes that respecting the boundaries of other families is the cornerstone of domestic virtue.

ai.literal: Not looking at another's wife is great strength of character; to the noble, is it only virtue? It is also exemplary conduct.
ai.translation: Not looking with desire at another's wife is a great strength of character; for the noble, it is not only a virtue but also exemplary conduct.
ai.modern: பிறனுடைய மனைவியை விரும்பாத பேராண்மையானது, சான்றோர்களுக்கு அறம் மட்டும் அன்று; அதுவே நிறைந்த ஒழுக்கமும் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme quality of not desiring another man's wife. It states that such restraint is not just a basic moral virtue (அறன்) for the noble, but it represents the highest form of strength of character (பேராண்மை) and exemplary conduct (ஒழுக்கு). The word 'பேராண்மை' (great manliness) is used here not as physical strength, but as the mental fortitude to control one's desires. For those of high character, this self-control is the very definition of noble conduct.

ai.translation: If you ask, 'Who are those worthy of virtue in this world surrounded by the dread ocean?' They are those who do not embrace the shoulders of a woman who belongs to another.
ai.modern: அச்சம் தரும் கடல் சூழ்ந்த இவ்வுலகத்தில், அறத்திற்கு உரியவர் யார் என்று கேட்டால், அவர் பிறனுக்கு உரியவளின் தோள்களைத் தீண்டாதவர் ஆவார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate standard of virtue in the world. The poet uses the phrase 'நாமநீர் வைப்பு' (the world surrounded by the terrifying, vast ocean) to establish a grand, global scale. Within this vast world, the highest moral excellence is attributed to those who possess the self-control to never embrace another man's wife ('பிறர்க்குரியாள் தோள்தோயாதார்'). Their restraint is marked as the defining qualification for true goodness.

words.gloss: one who does not abide by the limits of

ai.literal: Even if one who does not abide by the limits of virtue does deeds other than virtuous, not desiring the womanhood of another's wedded wife is good.
ai.translation: Even if a man does not walk in the path of virtue and commits other sins, it is still a saving grace if he does not lust after the wife of another.
ai.modern: அறநெறியைப் பின்பற்றாமல் ஒருவன் தீமைகளையே செய்து வந்தாலும், பிறனுடைய மனைவியின் பெண்மையை விரும்பாமல் இருப்பது அவனுக்கு நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the gravity of desiring another man's wife by comparing it to other vices. The poet states that even if a person fails to live by the rules of virtue ('அறன் வரையான்') and commits various wrongdoings ('அல்ல செயினும்'), he still retains a fundamental goodness if he refrains from desiring the womanhood of a married woman ('பிறன் வரையாள் பெண்மை நயவாமை'). The word 'வரையான்' refers to one who does not bound himself by moral laws, while 'வரையாள்' refers to a woman bound to another in marriage. By declaring this restraint as 'good' even for an otherwise unrighteous person, the couplet emphasizes that violating the sanctity of another's marriage is the worst of all transgressions.
